title: Is Codex getting worse since the €200 plan? I'm considering dropping it entirely.
author: Igafann
selftext:
I've been using Codex extensively for my indie metroidvania project, and honestly, I'm getting really disappointed.

I'm paying €100/month, and the usage limits are ridiculous. I burn through my quota so quickly that I sometimes need to buy extra credits almost every day. Last time I had 9% left and had to wait almost a week or pay again.

And the quality seems to be getting worse too. I ask it to improve something, and after several iterations, the result is often worse than what I started with. It removes details, oversimplifies things, and I spend more time correcting it.

Meanwhile, I'm using Claude Opus 5.5 on the exact same project, and it's excellent. Better results, fewer restrictions, and much less frustration.

I used to prefer Codex by far, so this isn't some Claude vs OpenAI fanboy thing.

I'm genuinely wondering if there's any connection with the €200 plan. Has the €100 tier become less attractive to push users toward the more expensive one? I don't know, but that's honestly how it feels.

At this point, I'm seriously considering removing Codex entirely from my development workflow and sticking with Claude.

Am I the only one experiencing this? Has anyone else noticed a decline in quality or value for money?

comments.author: Super_Range45
comments.body: These plans where never sustainable for Open AI and cutting quality was inevitable. Don't plan your small business around only need $100 per month for coding for the future.

comments.author: JDad67
comments.body: If you’re not getting value. Drop it. If you are getting value… keep it.

comments.author: MaqeSweden
comments.body:
Agreed, Astra is munching tokens like crazy, and 6.1 Sol is not as good as its cost compared to Claude.

I will step down to $100 plan or possibly $20 and using opus 5.5 and sonnet 5.5 (and haiku 5.5) for most I need to get done any given week. Still trying out Grok $20 and Antigravity $20, Kimi was not worth it. Opencode currently allows unlimited tokens for Muse Spark 1.3 which can do some easy tasks.

replies.author: Ok_Improvement_8735
replies.body: Hm, I just began using codex over claude code because I thought the opposite actually that claude code burns tokens faster. If I use Astra on xhigh without having to approve anything it can "work" for literally between 40 - 50 hours before the weekly limit hits (plus I have a handful of weekly resets banked with codex, just got another free one expiring nov 6th).

replies.author: MaqeSweden
replies.body:
Yeah main reason to keep codex is the free resets, wasn't it for those it'd be crazy expensive.

But things are shifting fast. 3 weeks ago I would not have preferred claude. This is why I want to keep Codex too, sometimes things shift big in a day when a new model comes out. Sometimes things shift without new models coming out.

replies.author: moo_sweden
replies.body:
Luna Max in insanely cheap though and can handle quite advanced coding tasks if specs are well thought out and the planning is done with Astra or Sol.   
3D asset creation is another beast though.

my latest project is GPT 6.0/6.1 and it came out fine: [https://chooon.itch.io/superhero-mayhem-simulator](https://chooon.itch.io/superhero-mayhem-simulator)

comments.author: daddywookie
comments.body:
I think it makes a huge difference how you set up your working environment. If you leave yourself in the hand of OpenAI/Anthropic then you'll always be chasing a moving target. 

On the other hand, set up your skills and references, develop a consistent production process and force yourself to work in small steps with manual play testing and the agents don't make as much of a difference.

comments.author: AMSolar
comments.body:
Brother are you for real still using astra when Sol 6.1 performs just as well for most things at 1/5 of the cost?

It's like paying $2,000 for a graphics card that's only 5% faster than a $400 card.

As soon as Sol 6.1 dropped I've never had to use Astra and I'm not sure it'll be ever worth it relative to Sol

And anthropic doesn't have anything in their lineup comparable to Sol 6.1 yet.

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: Codex recently cut the $200 plan to $100, so yes.

comments.author: detailteufel
comments.body: I can't prove it but all these "new model" releases we are seeing are just these AI companies putting everyone on the Q8 quant for a week and raising context window plus a handful of new tools for each release. Then after 2 weeks they scale it all back slowly until the next "model release", when you are already used to the AI being a donkey again and then the "new model" suddenly seems amazing. Rinse and repeat. Astra was great when it came out. Over the past weeks it has degraded so much it's basically just wasting usage at this point. Worse it spams my projects full of unnecessary shit and stealth applies ridiculous bullshit without asking.

comments.author: Kagemand
comments.body:
$100 seems trash right now, though I might need to keep it for work as Astra is probably still much better for writing consultant/policy white papers than Claude. 

I would prefer it if I could just use Opus 5.5 and get a x20 plan for everything instead…

replies.author: Upstairs_Tone_4227
replies.body: Is getting 2 separate 5x plans that work on the same project a viable route?

replies.body: That seems like bad value. I’ve been in that situation though because I wanted one private projects and one for work, in particular ChatGPT because it writes better. But if I could just lose dependence on ChatGPT, I would do 20x Claude… Seems like much better value.
